title: Impact of Institutional Ownership on Firm Value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using S&P 500 inclusion (z) as an instrument for institutional ownership (x) to estimate its causal effect on firm value (y).
- Why IV: Institutional ownership is endogenous to firm value (reverse causality; omitted variables such as governance quality). S&P 500 inclusion mechanically induces flows from index funds that raise institutional ownership but is plausibly exogenous to short-run valuation, conditional on controls.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Inclusion in the S&P 500 increases institutional ownership (Cov(z, x) ≠ 0). We verify via a strong first-stage F-statistic.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on controls, inclusion affects firm value only through its effect on institutional ownership (no direct effect through, e.g., publicity or liquidity). This is the main identifying restriction.
  - Independence: Conditional on controls, inclusion is as good as random with respect to unobserved determinants of firm value.
  - Monotonicity: No firms reduce institutional ownership because of inclusion (no defiers).
  - SUTVA: No spillovers across firms.
- Estimand: LATE of institutional ownership on firm value for compliers with respect to index inclusion.
- Note: Data appear as pooled firm-time observations without identifiers; we use heteroskedasticity-robust inference. With firm/time IDs, one would add fixed effects and cluster by firm.

## 2. R Code
```r
# IV analysis: S&P 500 inclusion (z) -> institutional ownership (x) -> firm value (y)
# Path: experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv

# 1) Setup --------------------------------------------------------------------
pkgs <- c("readr", "dplyr", "AER", "sandwich", "lmtest", "broom")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)

fmt <- function(x, d = 4) formatC(x, digits = d, format = "f")

# 2) Load data ----------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s80_data.csv"
dat <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Basic cleaning: keep required columns and drop missing
dat <- dat %>%
  select(y, x, z, controls) %>%
  mutate(
    z = as.integer(z),
    controls = as.numeric(controls),
    x = as.numeric(x),
    y = as.numeric(y)
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(y), is.finite(x), is.finite(z), is.finite(controls))

cat("Sample size (complete cases):", nrow(dat), "\n")
cat("Share included in S&P 500 (z=1):", fmt(mean(dat$z)), "\n\n")

# 3) Naive OLS (benchmark, not causal) ---------------------------------------
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))
ols_b  <- unname(ols_ct["x", "Estimate"])
ols_se <- unname(ols_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
ols_p  <- unname(ols_ct["x", "Pr(>|t|)"])
cat("Naive OLS (y ~ x + controls):\n",
    "  beta_x =", fmt(ols_b), 
    "  SE =", fmt(ols_se),
    "  p =", fmt(ols_p), "\n\n")

# 4) First stage: x on z and controls ----------------------------------------
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_ct <- coeftest(fs, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))
pi_z  <- unname(fs_ct["z", "Estimate"])
pi_se <- unname(fs_ct["z", "Std. Error"])
pi_t  <- unname(fs_ct["z", "t value"])
fs_F  <- as.numeric(pi_t^2)   # robust t^2 as an F for single excluded instrument
cat("First Stage (x ~ z + controls):\n",
    "  Effect of z on x =", fmt(pi_z),
    "  SE =", fmt(pi_se),
    "  t =", fmt(pi_t),
    "  Robust F (z) =", fmt(fs_F), "\n\n")

# 5) Reduced form: y on z and controls ---------------------------------------
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
rf_ct <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))
rf_b  <- unname(rf_ct["z", "Estimate"])
rf_se <- unname(rf_ct["z", "Std. Error"])
rf_p  <- unname(rf_ct["z", "Pr(>|t|)"])
cat("Reduced Form (y ~ z + controls):\n",
    "  Effect of z on y =", fmt(rf_b),
    "  SE =", fmt(rf_se),
    "  p =", fmt(rf_p), "\n\n")

# 6) 2SLS main specification --------------------------------------------------
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv, vcov. = iv_vcov)

iv_b  <- unname(iv_ct["x", "Estimate"])
iv_se <- unname(iv_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
iv_t  <- unname(iv_ct["x", "t value"])
iv_p  <- unname(iv_ct["x", "Pr(>|t|)"])
iv_ci <- iv_b + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * iv_se

cat("2SLS (y ~ x + controls | z + controls):\n",
    "  beta_x_IV =", fmt(iv_b),
    "  SE =", fmt(iv_se),
    "  t =", fmt(iv_t),
    "  p =", fmt(iv_p), "\n",
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(iv_ci[1]), ", ", fmt(iv_ci[2]), "]\n\n", sep = "")

# 2SLS diagnostics from AER (classical, not robust)
iv_sum <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
if (!is.null(iv_sum$diagnostics)) {
  cat("AER diagnostics (classical):\n")
  print(iv_sum$diagnostics)
  cat("\n")
}

# 7) Robustness checks --------------------------------------------------------
# 7a) Functional form: quadratic control
iv_poly <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + I(controls^2) | z + controls + I(controls^2), data = dat)
iv_poly_ct <- coeftest(iv_poly, vcov. = vcovHC(iv_poly, type = "HC1"))
iv_poly_b  <- unname(iv_poly_ct["x", "Estimate"])
iv_poly_se <- unname(iv_poly_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
iv_poly_ci <- iv_poly_b + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * iv_poly_se
cat("Robustness (Quadratic control):\n",
    "  beta_x_IV =", fmt(iv_poly_b),
    "  SE =", fmt(iv_poly_se),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(iv_poly_ci[1]), ", ", fmt(iv_poly_ci[2]), "]\n\n", sep = "")

# 7b) Outlier robustness: trim x at 1st/99th percentiles
lo <- as.numeric(quantile(dat$x, 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))
hi <- as.numeric(quantile(dat$x, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE))
dat_trim <- dat %>% filter(x >= lo, x <= hi)
iv_trim <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat_trim)
iv_trim_ct <- coeftest(iv_trim, vcov. = vcovHC(iv_trim, type = "HC1"))
iv_trim_b  <- unname(iv_trim_ct["x", "Estimate"])
iv_trim_se <- unname(iv_trim_ct["x", "Std. Error"])
iv_trim_ci <- iv_trim_b + c(-1, 1) * 1.96 * iv_trim_se
cat("Robustness (Trim x at 1%/99%):\n",
    "  beta_x_IV =", fmt(iv_trim_b),
    "  SE =", fmt(iv_trim_se),
    "  95% CI: [", fmt(iv_trim_ci[1]), ", ", fmt(iv_trim_ci[2]), "]\n\n", sep = "")

# 7c) Naive OLS vs IV comparison (direction and magnitudes)
cat("Comparison summary:\n",
    "  OLS beta_x =", fmt(ols_b), " (SE ", fmt(ols_se), ")\n",
    "  IV  beta_x =", fmt(iv_b),  " (SE ", fmt(iv_se), ")\n\n", sep = "")

# 8) Clear numerical result (main estimate) -----------------------------------
cat("MAIN RESULT (2SLS): Estimated causal effect of institutional ownership (x) on firm value (y) = ",
    fmt(iv_b), " (SE ", fmt(iv_se), "), 95% CI [", fmt(iv_ci[1]), ", ", fmt(iv_ci[2]), "].\n", sep = "")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Slightly negative. Increased institutional ownership driven by index inclusion is largely passive (index funds), which can dilute monitoring incentives or lead to mechanical trading. While inclusion can also improve liquidity and visibility (potentially positive), the local effect of passive inflows is often small and can be weakly negative for valuation once endogeneity is addressed.
- Magnitude: Modest. For a one-unit increase in x (institutional ownership in the dataset’s units), I expect the 2SLS coefficient on y to be in the range of approximately −0.1 to −0.3, with confidence intervals that may include small negatives near zero if the instrument is weak or the true effect is small.
- Diagnostics expectations:
  - First-stage: Positive and statistically meaningful effect of z on x (robust F ideally > 10).
  - Reduced form: Small negative coefficient of z on y.
  - IV vs OLS: OLS likely biased toward zero or positive; IV more negative.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use S&P 500 inclusion as an instrument for institutional ownership.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased institutional ownership, driven by index inclusion, leads to a decrease in firm value.
